claim.summary: On a smooth projective geometrically integral curve over a finite field, genus g, n distinct rational evaluation points, divisors A,G of nonnegative degrees a,m avoiding those points, t>=0, a>=t+g and n>a+m+t, recover any f in L(G) from its evaluations corrupted at <=t unknown positions. Solve N(P_i)=lambda(P_i)y_i with lambda in L(A), N in L(A+G). Nonzero solutions exist, every nonzero solution has lambda nonzero and N=lambda f identically, and kills every actual error. A second weighted evaluation system uniquely recovers f. If rational R avoids the points and supports of A,G and a>=t+2g, add lambda(R)=1; the system remains consistent and N(R)=f(R). With bases/evaluation matrices supplied, O(n^3) field operations and O(n^2) memory. Costs of producing those inputs are separate. This supplies geometric certificates for established bilinear error recovery, not a new decoder or a bounded-PC identification.
claim.assessment: Working geometric recovery application passed by the sole fresh-context medium reviewer: divisor bounds, every accepted solution, protected normalization, signal injectivity and dense-input cost checked. Established decoding mechanism, no novelty claim.

claim.summary: For a smooth projective geometrically integral curve X/k of genus g, divisor A and effective divisor E of degree e, deg A>=e+g gives a nonzero f in L(A-E). If a k-rational P avoids supports of A,E and deg A>=e+2g, one can choose f(P)=1. Standard Riemann-Roch and point-evaluation consequence: vanishing along E is as an O(A) section, and as a rational function when A/E supports are disjoint. Separate protected-value budget; no PC curve model or optimality assertion.

claim.summary: For finite-dimensional U,V,W,Z, bilinear beta:U x V to W, tester Q:W to Z, clean C<=V and errors E, assume Q beta(U,C)=0, rank beta_e<dim U, ker Q intersect beta(U,e)=0 for every e, and beta_a injective on C for every nonzero a. For y=c+e, any nonzero solution Q beta(a,y)=0 kills e and uniquely recovers c by a second linear system. Standard error-correcting pairs satisfy these conditions when (A*B) perpendicular C, dim A>t, d(B-perp)>t and d(A)+d(C)>n, yielding O(n^3) field operations with bases supplied. Reed-Solomon evaluations work for n>=k+2t.
